title: next-site

  label: Overview
---

One Next.js 16 app with Payload CMS 3 inside it, on Postgres. The site's owner
edits pages, images, menus and (with the shop) products and orders at
`/admin`; there is no separate backend.

```sh
stack new next-site ./kofi-bakery                # business website
stack new next-site ./ama-shop --with shop       # with a store
```

**Stack:** Next.js 16, React 19, Payload CMS 3 (Postgres adapter, Lexical
editor, form builder, SEO, search, redirects, ecommerce), Tailwind CSS 4 with
the house UI kit, OpenTelemetry and OpenObserve RUM. One Node server in Docker.

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Dev server | `yarn dev` on port 3000; the admin at `/admin` |
| Content model | `src/collections/`, `src/globals/`, page blocks in `src/blocks/` |
| Public site | `src/app/(app)/`; any CMS page renders at `/<slug>`, `/` is `home` |
| Database | Postgres through Payload; migrations in `src/migrations/` |
| Payments (shop) | adapters in `src/payments/`; `manual` built in |

## When to use it

For a site its owner runs: a business website, a portfolio, a small shop. When
the product needs an API of its own (mobile clients, background jobs, complex
domain logic), use [react-app](../react-app/) with [nest-api](../nest-api/)
instead.

## The shop

`--with shop` adds products with variants and stock, a cart, checkout,
customer accounts and guest order lookup. Prices are in one currency (GHS by
default, `src/lib/currency.ts`). The built-in `manual` payment method places
the order as **awaiting payment**, shows the payment instructions the owner
writes in Shop settings, and emails the customer and the owner; the owner marks
the order paid in the admin once the money arrives. Other payment providers
are adapters beside it (the project's `add-payment-provider` skill).
